question: Can a frozen black-box LM be improved by prepending retrieved documents, and can the retriever be tuned using the LM's own scores as supervision?
hypothesis: Adapting the retriever to the LM (rather than the LM to the retriever) finds documents that lower LM perplexity and beats an untuned retriever.
contributions: REPLUG, first retrieval-augmented framework for black-box large LMs
REPLUG LSR training scheme using LM scores as supervision for the retriever
Evaluations on language modeling, MMLU and open-domain QA across GPT, OPT, BLOOM up to 175B

method.summary: Top-k documents are retrieved with a dense dual-encoder (Contriever, cosine similarity, FAISS); each is prepended to the input in a separate LM pass and next-token probabilities are ensembled with softmax-of-similarity weights. REPLUG LSR fine-tunes the retriever by minimising KL between the retrieval likelihood and a softmax over the frozen LM's likelihood of the gold continuation per document.
method.task: language modeling (Pile BPB, Wikitext-103 perplexity), MMLU, open-domain QA (NQ, TriviaQA)

datasets.name: Pile training queries
datasets.split: first 128 tokens = input x, last 128 = continuation y
datasets.preprocessing: retrieval corpus documents do not overlap with documents the queries came from

datasets.name: Pile (eval)
datasets.preprocessing: retrieval corpus: random subsample of Pile train, 367M documents of 128 tokens; no extra dedup filtering

datasets.name: Natural Questions / TriviaQA (filtered)
datasets.split: few-shot (16 shots for Codex-based) and full-data

datasets.name: Wikitext-103
datasets.split: test; train set as retrieval corpus
datasets.source: Merity et al. (printed as Stephen et al. 2017)

models.name: Contriever
models.architecture: dense dual encoder, mean pooling of last hidden states, cosine similarity

other.REPLUG_LSR: retriever initialised from Contriever and fine-tuned

training.objective: KL(P_R(d|x) || Q_LM(d|x,y)) over top-20 retrieved docs; only retriever updated, LM frozen; both softmaxes temperature 0.1

other.index_refresh: document embeddings recomputed and FAISS index rebuilt every 3k steps
other.gamma_beta: temperature of 0.1 for retrieval and LM likelihoods (single value stated)

inference.samples: one run per setting; no seeds or variance reported
inference.prompting: MMLU 5-shot direct prompting with 'Knowledge: ... Question: ... Answer:' format; open-domain QA 16-shot for Codex
inference.retrieval: top-10 documents, each prepended separately, probabilities ensembled; 128-token context as retrieval query for language modeling; test question as query for MMLU/QA

parameters.lambda: softmax of cosine similarity over top-k

metrics.definition: bits per UTF-8 encoded byte on Pile subsets

results.setup: Codex (code-davinci-002) 175B, top-10 Wikipedia (Dec 2018) passages, ensemble, 5-shot direct prompting
results.table: Table 2, row Codex + REPLUG LSR, column All

results.claim: Untuned REPLUG (Contriever) raises Codex MMLU to 71.4, relative +4.5%.
results.table: Table 2, row Codex + REPLUG, column All

results.claim: REPLUG and REPLUG LSR improve Codex on MMLU by 4.5% and 5.1% (relative).
results.quote: improve the original Codex model by 4.5% and 5.1%, respectively

results.claim: On Pile bits-per-byte, REPLUG LSR gives 7.7% average improvement over 8 baseline LMs vs 4.7% for REPLUG.
results.setup: 8 LMs (GPT-2 S/M/L/XL, GPT-3 Ada/Babbage/Curie/Davinci), top-10 docs ensembled, 128-token retrieval context, 367M-doc corpus from Pile train

limits: Authors concede REPLUG lacks interpretability: unclear when the model relies on retrieved or parametric knowledge.
Tuned only with Curie supervision and used for other LMs; Flan-PaLM and PaLM not accessible, so untested.
Requires k forward passes and token probabilities from the LM.
No seeds, variance, or significance; hardware and compute for LSR training unstated; code link not in the text.
Full-data finetuned retrieval LMs still beat it on NQ/TQA.
